role: Explains why macOS CI is manual-dispatch only, what gates run where (gates.yml on ubuntu, make ci locally), the gate self-verification harnesses and the costs accepted.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically
units.does: Claims every macOS workflow is workflow_dispatch only; gates.yml runs the bash/python gates (including the code map) on every push to main and every pull request on ubuntu, and that job is the one status check main requires before a merge. Code: ci.yml, performance.yml, security.yml and testflight.yml trigger on workflow_dispatch (ci.yml also workflow_call); gates.yml triggers on push to branches [main], pull_request and workflow_dispatch on ubuntu-latest and has the step "Code map is current". The required check is a repository ruleset setting, not visible in the repo.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > The arithmetic
units.does: Claims macOS minutes bill at 10x and a full run (tests, thread-sanitizer, lint-and-budgets) is ~108 wall minutes / ~1,080 billable, measured on run 33202282889, and that on a push trigger the allowance would be gone in under a week. ci.yml's header comment records the same measurement (1083 billable).

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here
units.does: Claims `make ci` runs every gate plus the full test suite with the identical scripts and .ci budget files CI uses. Makefile:272 ci lists the static gates, verify-gates and test-coverage; it does not include the thread-sanitizer target (Makefile:162) that ci.yml runs as its own job.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > Running CI locally before paying for it
units.does: Claims make ci-local / ci-local-unit run scripts/simulate_ci.sh, which parses ci.yml and executes its run: blocks in order, treating unknown steps as errors and skipping only Xcode selection and brew install; should run after committing because the ratchet compares HEAD to HEAD~1. Makefile:260/263 call simulate_ci.sh (with --scope unit); simulate_ci.sh loads ci.yml via yaml.safe_load and has skip patterns for sudo xcode-select and brew install/update/tap.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > The gates
units.does: Claims the listed gate groups (including a Change tracking row: the code map's records current with their code, records whose callees changed listed for re-check) are all scripts in scripts/ run identically by make ci, make ci-local and Actions; every gate except check_coverage.sh and check_thread_sanitizer.sh has a plant in verify_gates_fail.sh, whose meta-check enumerates scripts/check_*.sh and enforce_*.sh failing on any without a plant or exemption; check_budget_monotonicity.sh skips without a baseline and takes HEAD to check uncommitted edits. Code: verify_gates_fail.sh loops over check_*/enforce_* and errors on unplanted gates; check_budget_monotonicity.sh exits 0 without a baseline (no_baseline) and accepts a ref argument.
calls: .github/workflows/ci.yml::step lint-and-budgets/Every gate is wired into CI

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > Three questions, not one
units.does: Claims each gate is checked three ways: verify_gates_fail.sh (goes red), check_gate_preflight.sh (fails closed), check_gates_wired.sh (wired into ci.yml). All three scripts exist; ci.yml has 'Gates actually fail', 'Gates fail closed' and 'Every gate is wired into CI' steps.
calls: .github/workflows/ci.yml::step lint-and-budgets/Every gate is wired into CI

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > Two things must not read the tree at the same time
units.does: Claims verify_gates_fail.sh and verify_tests_fail.sh mutate tracked source and restore in an EXIT trap, both take .git/emuqu-tree-mutation.lock, simulate_ci.sh refuses to start while it is held, and a stale lock is taken over with a warning; check_no_leaked_mutations.sh is the backstop for a killed run. Code: both harnesses source scripts/lib/preflight.sh and call gate_acquire_tree_lock (verify_gates_fail.sh:37, verify_tests_fail.sh:74) with release in the EXIT trap; GATE_TREE_LOCK defaults to <git dir>/emuqu-tree-mutation.lock (falling back to TMPDIR when no git dir); simulate_ci.sh:47 calls gate_require_unmutated_tree; preflight.sh:159 warns on a stale lock.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > The tests are checked too, not just the code
units.does: Claims verify_tests_fail.sh mutates a chosen set of behaviours (pNN50 threshold, SDNN, RMSSD, NP fourth root, recovery label comparison, encrypted-write branch) and requires the suite to catch each; logic lifted out of large types gets its own mutations; TrackBackupWatermark's test drops one cursor at a time with a mutation per clause, and the recovery merge's more-beats tie-break is its own function with its own test because DataSourceSelector answers first. verify_tests_fail.sh defines mutate(), a pnn50_threshold mutation of TimeDomainAnalysis 'abs($0) > 50' -> 75 against EmuquTests/TimeDomainTests, and TrackBackupWatermark mutations.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > Where to point it next: at the comments that claim something is subtle
units.does: Claims comments that call behaviour subtle are mutation leads: tests pin the three RRDataImporter+CSV.rrValue asymmetries with permanent mutations; WorkoutMileMarkerEngine's zone label must use max HR, not session peak, as the denominator, with tests and a mutation swapping it back; HealthExportIdentity's tests assert no metric's delete reaches another metric's or session's samples; verify_tests_fail.sh needs a build per mutation so it is not in make ci. Named units exist; verify_tests_fail.sh has RRDataImporter+CSV, HealthExportIdentity and zone_label_uses_session_peak_as_denominator cases and is not a dependency of the Makefile ci target.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > Runs are scoped, because a full one is expensive
units.does: Claims ci.yml takes a dispatch scope gates (default, ~14 billable), unit (~300), full (~1080), and workflow_call defaults to full so the TestFlight gate runs everything. Code: ci.yml workflow_dispatch input scope default gates with those options; workflow_call input scope default full; testflight.yml quality-gate uses ./.github/workflows/ci.yml.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What actually enforces quality here > The compiler is one of the gates
units.does: Claims run_tests_with_coverage.sh passes -warn-long-expression-type-checking and -warn-long-function-bodies, the spec-conformance scan covers the whole app target (including Emuqu/EmuquApp.swift, where verify_gates_fail.sh plants a violation), there are zero swiftlint:disable directives in Emuqu/Sources, and check_budget_monotonicity.sh fails unjustified raises. Code: run_tests_with_coverage.sh:221 TYPE_CHECK_FLAGS with =4000/=6000; grep finds 0 swiftlint:disable in Emuqu/Sources.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > Where GitHub Actions is still used
units.does: Claims testflight.yml calls ci.yml as a reusable workflow and security.yml (CodeQL) is on demand. Code: testflight.yml quality-gate job uses ci.yml; security.yml is workflow_dispatch with codeql and dependency-review jobs.

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > What this posture does *not* claim
units.does: no behavioural claim: lists accepted costs, smaller than a CI system that cannot run, (no automated gate before main, no independent verification, no third-party record).

units.key: § CI posture — why the macOS suite does not run automatically > For reviewers
units.does: Tells reviewers that the macOS suite not running automatically is intended, and that main is protected by one required check, the Linux gates.yml job, with nothing needing macOS required; that macOS jobs should become required only after budget and a green run, which the Linux job has passed. Claims evidence_report.sh prints enforced ceilings (--json for machine output) without builds; sbom.spdx.json covers the app plus 11 resolved packages and make sbom-check fails when stale; the SBOM is unsigned with no build provenance. Code: sbom.spdx.json has 12 packages (app + 11); Makefile sbom-check. The required check is a repository ruleset setting, not visible in the repo.
